learning_outcomes.text: Understand and be able to apply the basic concepts of linear algebra.
Know the basics of statistics and their applications.
Understand the terminology, notation, and methods of Mathematics.
Know specific software for solving mathematical problems.
Be able to use abstraction mechanisms as a tool to help solve real-world problems.

syllabus_topics: Descriptive Statistics - Regression and correlation in two variables
Linear Algebra - Vector spaces, matrices, and determinants
Linear Algebra - Systems of Linear Equations
Linear Algebra - Matrix Diagonalization: eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Jordan forms.
Computer Practices - Handling a Computer Application - Creating, importing, and modifying data files. Working with large databases.

Computer Practices - Performing statistical calculations and representing graphs with unidimensional and bidimensional statistical variables. Obtaining linear and non-linear regression models for predictions and assessing their reliability.
Computer Practices - Calculating probabilities with different discrete and continuous probability functions for problem-solving applications.
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, a minimum of 4 out of 10 on the final exam is required; otherwise, the total grade is FAIL, capped at 4.5 points. If this minimum is met, the final grade is the weighted sum of observation techniques (25%), written tests (60%), and practical reports (15%). For the extraordinary call, observation techniques and practical reports are recoverable through exams. The final grade is the maximum of two formulas: (25% course observation + 60% extraordinary final exam + 15% practical reports) or (85% extraordinary final exam + 15% practical reports), with a mandatory minimum of 4 out of 10 on the extraordinary final exam to pass.
